summary.tldr: Expands some victim rights under the Canadian Victims Bill of Rights and sets out a federal plan for training, complaints and implementation.
what_it_does: Changes several information rights so victims would get certain information without having to ask for it, instead of only on request.
Adds a right to access legal, social, medical and psychological services that fit a victim’s needs and circumstances.
Adds a right to reparations, including access to restorative justice programs and to have the court consider a restitution order.
Adds a right for victims who get restitution orders to get help entering and enforcing those orders.
States that the Act cannot be applied to take away victims’ rights to access to justice and procedural fairness in the criminal justice system.
Requires the Minister of Justice to develop victim-rights training, create an implementation framework, table a report in Parliament, and publish it online.
who_it_affects: Federal Ombudsperson for Victims of Crime
summary.background: The bill amends the Canadian Victims Bill of Rights and adds a framework for putting those rights into practice.
